title: feat(plugin-detail): row caps admit only a positive integer number, and warn on refusal (objectui#10145)
body:
Closes #10145

Clause-②: no (it narrows, per ruling 5816948508)

Executes ruling 5816948508 (batch #222 item 2, letter A, STOP; maintainer 「同意」): the row-cap renderers read what the contract reads.

## What changed

- `normalizeLimit` (`recordActivityFeed.ts`, shared by `record:activity`, `record:chatter`, `record:discussion`) and `normalizeHistoryLimit` (`record-history.tsx`) no longer run `Number(value)`. Each reads one predicate: `typeof value === 'number' && Number.isInteger(value) && value > 0`. This is the same predicate the three objectui#9925 read points (reference rail, kanban, timeline) already use.
- Every other authored value falls back to the block default (20 or 50). The renderer then logs one `console.warn` from an effect keyed on the message, the objectui#9925 channel. The warning names the block and spells the raw value with its type, for example `[ObjectUI] record:history row cap: declared limit: "5" (string), ...`. `undefined` and `null` (unauthored) stay silent.
- **1.5, 0, -3, NaN, Infinity**: I measured these on `origin/main` before the edit, and they already fell back (`Number.isInteger` / `> 0`). Their fallback is unchanged, and they now warn as well. The evidence: objectui#10097 ruled A ("always warn", comment 5807911435) for exactly these two silent read points, and it asks that the silence pin not survive. Warning only on the newly refused shapes would have left the family with two answers again. objectui#10097 remains open for the PM to reconcile. This PR covers its two silent read points and adds no warning anywhere else.
- Docs: the `limit` row in `content/docs/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx` now states the rule.
- Changeset `.changeset/10145-row-cap-admits-only-numbers.md`: `minor` on `@object-ui/plugin-detail`, with a migration note (stored string `limit` drops to the default and warns).

## Census (ruling item 5), on `origin/main` 8b1f06619

`git grep` for `Number(` over `packages/*/src` (excluding tests), then for every `limit` / `pageSize` / `maxRows` read. I read each hit:

| read point | shape | action |
|---|---|---|
| `normalizeLimit` via `record-activity.tsx` (`read('limit')`) | `Number(value)` | changed |
| `normalizeLimit` via `record-chatter.tsx` (`feed?.limit`, both `record:chatter` and `record:discussion`) | same function | changed (warns under its own block name) |
| `normalizeHistoryLimit` (`record-history.tsx`) | `Number(value)` | changed |
| `record-reference-rail.tsx`, `plugin-kanban` `ObjectKanban.tsx`, `plugin-timeline` `ObjectTimeline.tsx`, `plugin-form` `LineItemsPanel.tsx` (`isUsableRowLimit`) | already `typeof === 'number'` | none needed |
| `record-related-list.tsx` | already `typeof schema.limit === 'number' && > 0` | none (different shape; admits a fraction, see notes) |
| `toaster.tsx` `limit`, `DatasetWidget.tsx` `options.limit` | already `typeof === 'number'` | none |
| `app-shell` `entitlements.ts` `Number(details?.limit)` | server entitlement payload, not a spec row cap | none, different key |
| `data-list.tsx` `props.limit`, `record-picker.tsx` `limit ?? 50`, `ElementDataSourceGate` / `element-data-source.ts` `config.limit` | no coercion (pass-through) | none, different shape |

So there are **2 resolvers of the same shape, serving 4 block types**, and both are covered here.

## Spec check

- `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 (installed): `RecordActivityProps`, `RecordHistoryProps` and `RecordChatterProps.feed` `safeParse` answer `invalid_type` for `'5'`, `' 5 '`, `'0x10'`, `true` and `[7]` (and for `1.5`), `too_small` for `0` and `-3`, and OK for `5`.
- objectstack `origin/main` e8f163f `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`: RecordActivity `limit: z.number().int().positive().default(20)`, RecordHistory `limit: z.number().int().positive().optional()`.

## Pins, flipped (not deleted), with lit controls kept

- `recordActivityFeed.test.ts`: `normalizeLimit('5')` now asserts `DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_LIMIT` (was 5). Lit control: `normalizeLimit(5)` is 5.
- `recordActivityFeed.rowLimitRefusal-10096.test.tsx`: the helper numeric-string control (`'5'`, `' 7 '`) now asserts the default, plus `'0x10'`, `true` and `[7]`, with lit `5` and `7`. The wire `topFor({ limit: '5' })` now asserts `RENDERER_DEFAULT + 1` (was 6), with a new lit control `topFor({ limit: 5 })` of 6. The silence pin is flipped to a warning pin (`it.each` over 8 refused values, 1 warning each, naming `record:activity` and the typed raw value), with a no-warning control for usable and absent caps.
- `record-history.rowLimitRefusal-10005.test.tsx`: the wire `'5'` now asserts `RENDERER_DEFAULT` (was 5), plus `' 5 '`, `'0x10'`, `true` and `[7]`, with lit `limit: 5` passing through. The silence pin is flipped to a warning pin (10 refused values), with a no-warning control.
- New `record-chatter.rowLimitRefusal-10145.test.tsx`: `record:chatter` and `record:discussion`. `feed.limit: 2` shows 2 rows silently (lit). `'2'`, `' 2 '`, `true` and `[2]` show all 6 rows with one warning naming the block.

## Reverse verification (at the committed head)

I restored the `Number(value)` body in `normalizeHistoryLimit` only. Proof it landed on disk: `grep -c 'const n = Number(value);'` answered 1, and the removed line answered 0. I then ran the history pin file: **8 failed | 16 passed (24)**. The 8 red are exactly the flipped string/boolean/array cases and their warnings. The lit controls and the number-valued refusals stayed green. I restored with `git checkout HEAD --`: `git diff HEAD` is 0 bytes, and the blob hash equals the HEAD blob (`baa1324e`).

## Gates (head 5cdeedc74)

- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/plugin-detail^...' build`: exit 0 (12 of 47 projects in scope).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, and the latter includes the tests): exit 0.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/`: 55 files, 657 tests passed.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the 8 changed TS files: 0 errors. Warnings per file match the base; the new test file carries 2 `no-explicit-any` warnings, the same `items as any` shape as its siblings.
- `check-changeset-presence`: pass. `check-changeset-no-major`: pass. `check:new-line-citations`: `0 new citation(s)`. `check:control-bytes`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:changeset-claims` and `check:pending-changeset-literals`: pass.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:doc-snippets` and `check:doc-examples`. Both exited 2 with PRECONDITION NOT MET, because they need a 34-package build. The docs edit is one table cell of prose with no code fence. Declared to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- `record-related-list.tsx` admits a positive NON-integer `limit` (`typeof === 'number' && > 0`, no integer check), and refuses silently. That is a different shape from this card (the number/non-number question is already answered there), so it is left untouched.
- The per-file `formatAuthoredLimit` / `isUsable*` predicate is now spelled at 6 sites across 4 packages. Consolidating it is out of scope.
